speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first began? I would also like to know if you have recently started any new medications, particularly for psychiatric conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is good to hear your psychiatric symptoms are improving, but I need to understand the nature of these new movements. Are the movements rhythmic and involuntary, such as grimacing, sticking out your tongue, or wriggling, and do they occur continuously or come in bursts?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of restlessness, fidgeting, and pacing, this sounds very much like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To help us determine the best way to manage this, have you tried reducing your dose or switching medications yet, and is the restlessness constant throughout the day or does it fluctuate?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have enough information to make a clinical determination. The patient's symptoms of inner restlessness, pacing, and fidgeting are classic presentations of akathisia, which is a known side effect of the risperidone he started two months ago for schizophrenia.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to risperidone use
